title: Mapping enhancer-gene regulatory interactions from single-cell data.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed both CRISPR benchmark TSVs (training: 10,356 rows x 42 columns, 471 Regulated=True, all K562, 3 screens; held-out: 4,378 rows, 190 positives across 5 cell types: K562 118, HCT116 34, GM12878 16, WTC11 15, Jurkat 7). No missing values, 0 duplicate element-gene keys, Regulated exactly equals Significant & EffectSize<0. 0 held-out K562 elements overlap a training element for the same gene, but 1,479/1,918 held-out K562 rows share a gene with training. Computed a distance-to-TSS (transcription start site) baseline: AUPRC (area under the precision-recall curve) 0.438 on training, 0.31-0.85 per held-out cell type. Listed all 5 Zenodo records (code only, MIT/GPL-3.0, 3-269 MB).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The scE2G single-cell features (from 10x Multiome ATAC/RNA data) were not opened; their locations sit in Supplementary Table 6, which was not retrievable (Europe PMC supplement endpoint timed out). scE2G's absolute AUPRC was not found in the text (only deltas, e.g. -0.022 vs ENCODE-rE2G). ENCODE-rE2G's AUPRC 0.63-0.66 and AlphaGenome's results come from search-result snippets, not papers I read in full.

a1_downloadable.note: Both CRISPR benchmark TSVs downloaded from GitHub without login (1.0 MB and 0.37 MB gzipped); code on Zenodo under MIT licence. Checked in files.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: 'Regulated' (boolean) is a column in the downloaded file, alongside EffectSize and pValueAdjusted. Nothing has to be constructed. Checked in files.

a3_inputs_present.note: Element coordinates (GRCh38), gene TSS (transcription start site) coordinates, Ensembl IDs, distance and bulk K562 chromatin features (H3K27ac, DNase, CTCF) are in the table. The paper's own single-cell features need separate Multiome processing; DNA sequence would be pulled from the reference genome by coordinate (no lookups).

a4_units_stated.note: EffectSize is fractional change in expression, distance in base pairs, chromatin signal in RPM (reads per million); units are implied by column names and consistent across rows. Checked in files.

a5_enough_rows.note: 10,356 training pairs with 471 positives (classification), plus 4,378 held-out pairs with 190 positives. Per held-out cell type the positives are tiny (Jurkat 7, WTC11 15).

a6_fits_laptop.note: The tabular baseline is trivial on CPU. Sequence-model features (Borzoi, AlphaGenome) over 1 Mb windows would be slow on CPU and are optional.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Paper says '>10,000 evaluated element-gene pairs' and 466 positives; the file has 10,356 pairs and 471 positives. Small gap (5 positives), probably a file revision; not checked further.

a8_label_provenance.note: Label is measured: CRISPR interference knockdown of the element followed by measuring the gene's expression (FlowFISH or Perturb-seq), with power filtering. It is not a model output, and none of the feature columns is computed from it.

B1.why: One 10,356-row training table; the held-out table has the identical 42-column schema. Seen in files.

B2.why: Both gzipped TSVs parsed first try with pandas; zero missing values.

B3.why: Labels from different screen types (FlowFISH, Perturb-seq, DC-TAP-seq) harmonised by authors; prevalence varies 0.8%-24% by cell type.

B4.why: No censored values; underpowered pairs already removed (ValidConnection all True). Seen in files.

B5.why: 0 duplicate element-gene keys in either file; no exact train/held-out overlap.

B6.why: Column names are self-explanatory but I did not find or read a column dictionary.

C1.why: Cell-type transfer is informative, but the paper and ENCODE-rE2G already report it.

C2.why: scE2G, ENCODE-rE2G, ABC, AlphaGenome, MPRabc all open and evaluated on this exact benchmark.

C3.why: Only weak angle: calibrated or sequence-based transfer to held-out cell types, already partly explored.

C4.why: Ground truth needs CRISPR screens per cell type, which are expensive lab assays.

C5.why: Published AUPRCs exist (ENCODE-rE2G ~0.63-0.66); distance baseline computed here at 0.438.

D1.why: Borzoi and AlphaGenome DNA sequence models have downloadable weights.

D2.why: Scoring 10k element deletions in 0.5-1 Mb windows is slow on CPU; a GPU is practical.

D3.why: AlphaGenome weights non-commercial; Borzoi believed permissive (not checked here).

E1.why: Hold out chromosomes or genes; separate held-out cell-type file exists. Seen in files.

E2.why: 2,113 genes, 23 chromosomes, 5 held-out cell types in the files.

E3.why: Distance-to-TSS baseline computed: AUPRC 0.438 vs 0.045 prevalence.

E4.why: No replicate measurements in the table; only power columns.

E5.why: Distance and H3K27ac known to predict enhancer effects; positives median 26 kb vs 387 kb.

E6.why: Label shuffle and feature-block ablation trivial on a 10k-row table.

E7.why: Held-out CRISPR file (5 cell types), eQTL Catalogue fine-mapped eQTLs, UK Biobank GWAS.

E8.why: CRISPR_comparison benchmark pipeline open on GitHub/Zenodo to reproduce published AUPRCs.

G1.why: GRCh38 coordinates and Ensembl gene IDs present in files.

G2.why: eQTL Catalogue v7 fine-mapped eQTLs and ENCODE chromatin tracks join on coordinates.

G3.why: Elements overlap multiple variants or peaks; collapse rule needed.

G4.why: CRISPR plus eQTL combination already done by this paper and ENCODE-rE2G.

H1.why: 9,885 negatives vs 471 positives, all power-filtered. Seen in files.

H2.why: Training is K562 only (one leukaemia line); held-out covers 5 cell lines.

H3.why: Claim stated precisely below, restricted to tested elements within ~2 Mb.

H4.why: Paper explicitly names the 466 positives and K562-only training as limitations.

I1.why: Engreitz lab and IGVF consortium build and use these enhancer-gene maps.

I2.why: Better maps marginally change which variant-gene links get tested.

I3.why: AUPRC roughly matches ranking links for follow-up; precision at fixed recall closer.

I4.why: Distance alone reaches AUPRC 0.44; trained models reach ~0.63-0.66, so ML helps somewhat.

J1.why: Real modelling: imbalanced classification, grouped splits, cell-type transfer, sequence-model features.

J2.why: Enhancer biology intuition needed; distance and H3K27ac priors help sanity-check.

J3.why: A re-run benchmark is shareable at every stage.

J4.why: No budget stated yet; a two-week cap is suggested.

J5.why: Kill condition proposed below but not yet written in NOTES.md.

existing_models.name: scE2G (this paper), logistic-regression classifier on single-cell ATAC/Multiome features
existing_models.score_and_split: Trained on K562 CRISPR with chromosome-held-out CV; Multiome version within -0.022 AUPRC of ENCODE-rE2G (absolute value not found in text); also tested on 5 held-out cell types.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Only 466 positives, K562-only training, 'modest' performance on other cell types; 'we have not yet reached the maximum performance achievable in this CRISPR dataset.'

existing_models.name: ENCODE-rE2G, logistic regression on DNase-seq plus ABC features
existing_models.score_and_split: AUPRC 0.63-0.66 on the K562 CRISPR set vs ABC 0.55-0.56 (from search snippet of the Nature 2026 paper).

existing_models.name: AlphaGenome, DNA sequence-to-function model (zero-shot)
existing_models.score_and_split: Zero-shot within 1% AUPRC of ENCODE-rE2G-extended on the ENCODE-rE2G CRISPR set (search snippet).

existing_models.name: MPRabc, ABC model informed by massively parallel reporter assays (NAR 2026)
existing_models.score_and_split: AUPRC 0.707 on the same benchmarking pipeline (search snippet).

existing_models.name: Genomics x AI blog benchmark of Enformer, Borzoi, NTv3, AlphaGenome
existing_models.score_and_split: Zero-shot Pearson r 0.67 (Fulco) and 0.45 (Gasperini) for AlphaGenome on K562 CRISPRi effect sizes.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: All models underpredict knockdown magnitude, worsening with distance from the TSS.

backbone.name: Borzoi (or Flashzoi), a DNA sequence-to-expression model; AlphaGenome as alternative
backbone.hardware: CPU possible but slow for ~10k in-silico deletions in 524 kb windows; a GPU is practical
backbone.licence: Borzoi believed Apache-2.0 (not verified); AlphaGenome non-commercial

integration.partner_dataset: eQTL Catalogue v7 fine-mapped eQTLs; ENCODE chromatin tracks for the held-out cell lines
integration.join_key: GRCh38 genomic coordinates + Ensembl gene ID
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do enhancer-gene rules learned from CRISPR screens in one leukaemia line explain natural genetic variation in gene expression across tissues? (Already addressed by this paper and ENCODE-rE2G.)

controls.positive_control: Distance to TSS alone must give AUPRC near 0.44 on training data (verified here); H3K27ac signal should add to it.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle Regulated labels within chromosome and confirm AUPRC falls to the 0.045 prevalence.
controls.external_validation: Held-out CRISPR file covering WTC11, HCT116, GM12878, Jurkat and new K562 DC-TAP-seq screens (4,378 pairs, verified); fine-mapped eQTLs.

honest_claim_h3: Among candidate elements within ~2 Mb that someone chose to perturb by CRISPR interference, mostly in K562 cells, the model ranks which ones measurably reduce a nearby gene's expression.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use an element's chromatin marks, DNA sequence and distance to a gene to predict whether silencing that element lowers the gene's expression.
plain_idea.train_on: 10,356 element-gene pairs tested by CRISPR in K562 leukaemia cells (verified), each with distance and chromatin-signal columns, optionally plus DNA-sequence model scores.
plain_idea.predict: Whether the gene's expression dropped significantly when the element was silenced by CRISPR interference, measured by FlowFISH or single-cell RNA sequencing in the original screens.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Geneticists linking non-coding disease variants to genes need these maps; but several open models already do this on the same data, so the gain would be marginal.

more_or_better_data.why: We would use the same 10,356 K562 pairs and 4,378 held-out pairs that scE2G, ENCODE-rE2G and AlphaGenome were all evaluated on.

confidence_score.why: The power columns (PowerAtEffectSize10-50) could support per-pair confidence, but there are no replicates and only 7-34 positives in most held-out cell types.

models_beatable.why: scE2G and ENCODE-rE2G are 2026 papers with chromosome-held-out and held-out-cell-type evaluation; MPRabc reports 0.707 AUPRC; AlphaGenome matches them zero-shot.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No new accessible CRISPR data beyond the held-out file, which is already used for testing; adding eQTLs measures a different quantity.

label_elsewhere.sources: The EngreitzLab CRISPR_comparison resource itself (training and held-out files, opened); IGVF consortium CRISPR screens and the eQTL Catalogue (known resources; eQTLs are a proxy label, not the same measurement).
label_elsewhere.why: The held-out file gives a ready external test on 5 cell types, but beyond that, measured enhancer-gene CRISPR labels are scarce.

risks: 1,479 of 1,918 held-out K562 rows share a target gene with training, so gene-level effects (e.g., highly expressed GATA1, 212 rows) can leak.
Overlapping or adjacent elements tested against the same gene in different screens can sit on both sides of a random split.
Screen of origin (Gasperini 6.8% positive vs Schraivogel 1.8%) correlates with the label, so screen-specific features could act as a batch shortcut.
leakage_plan.split: Hold out whole chromosomes (column 'chrom', seen in files) for cross-validation, then test once on the held-out-cell-type file grouped by 'CellType' (seen).
checks: Shuffle Regulated within chromosome and confirm AUPRC collapses to prevalence (0.045).
Train on distanceToTSS alone and report the gain of every other feature over the 0.438 baseline.
Report AUPRC separately for held-out K562 genes seen versus unseen in training.
leakage_plan.verdict: Manageable: chromosome and cell-type columns exist, and the benchmark pipeline already enforces sensible splits.

success_criteria.metric: AUPRC on the held-out-cell-type file pooled over non-K562 cell types, since users rank candidate links for follow-up in new cell types.
success_criteria.baselines: Distance-to-TSS: 0.31 (HCT116), 0.46 (WTC11), 0.49 (Jurkat), 0.85 (GM12878), computed here; scE2G and ENCODE-rE2G held-out numbers via the open pipeline (not yet reproduced).
success_criteria.success: Pooled held-out non-K562 AUPRC at least 0.05 above ENCODE-rE2G run through the same pipeline.
success_criteria.kill: If after one week the model is not at least 0.03 AUPRC better than ENCODE-rE2G on held-out cell types, stop.

ambitious.why: Publishes enhancer-gene methods; would need a clear, robust gain on held-out cell types over scE2G and ENCODE-rE2G.

realistic.why: Takes benchmark notes comparing sequence-model features against chromatin-based linkers on a shared CRISPR benchmark.

fallback.journal: bioRxiv preprint plus a machine-learning-in-genomics workshop
fallback.why: A negative result ('sequence models add nothing beyond distance in new cell types') fits a workshop note.

pitch.headline: A 10,356-pair CRISPR-measured enhancer-gene table that parses in one line, plus a 4,378-pair test set from 5 other cell types.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: Labels are direct CRISPR knockdown measurements, power-filtered, with 0 missing values and 0 duplicate keys (verified), released under MIT-licensed code.
pitch.the_win: A sequence-model head beating ENCODE-rE2G's held-out-cell-type AUPRC by 0.05; unlikely given AlphaGenome already matches it zero-shot.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: A clean measurement of how much beyond distance-to-gene (AUPRC 0.44, verified) any feature adds in new cell types: useful, but largely already reported.
pitch.who_wants_it: Engreitz lab and IGVF consortium groups choosing which enhancer-gene model to apply to new single-cell atlases.

ml_idea: Train on K562 CRISPR pairs with distance, bulk chromatin and frozen Borzoi/AlphaGenome deletion scores; evaluate transfer to the 5 held-out cell types with the open CRISPR_comparison pipeline. Best used as a clean learning project, not a publication edge.

effort.compute_note: Tables loaded and baselines computed in seconds (timed informally); sequence-model scoring cost not estimated because CPU throughput for 524 kb-1 Mb windows is unknown.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count positives per held-out cell type (done: Jurkat 7, WTC11 15, GM12878 16), which already limits per-cell-type claims; next, reproduce ENCODE-rE2G's held-out AUPRC with the open pipeline.

verdict_reason: Data is fully model-ready and passes Part A in the files, but this exact benchmark is saturated: scE2G, ENCODE-rE2G, ABC, MPRabc and AlphaGenome are open and honestly evaluated on it, and held-out cell types have only 7-34 positives. Good for learning, weak publication edge.
